evals.prompt: Plan only, no framework supplied. A singleton background worker captures a request-scoped database session and tenant through a factory closure. Async initialization can fail after opening an owned client; another client is externally supplied and borrowed. A teammate suggests Lazy lookup through a global provider to fix the lifetime/cycle problems. Define injection boundaries, job scopes, resource ownership, safe failure/cancellation and meaningful tests without inventing container APIs. Keep Factory/Builder/composition-root selection with the existing construction guide.
evals.expected_output: Trace transitive capture, create operation-owned scopes per job, preserve tenant isolation, reject locator/lazy workarounds, and assign cleanup/validation without redesigning construction.
assertions: Identifies that a closure or Lazy does not fix a captured shorter-lived dependency.
Defines job-scoped execution, explicit per-job tenant context and non-escaping scoped resources.
Cleans up owned partial initialization while preserving borrowed clients and primary failure/cancellation semantics.
Proposes scope/isolation and actual wiring checks without inventing framework APIs or competing construction ownership.

evals.prompt: Conceptual only. A service already receives one concrete mail-sending callable from bootstrap, and a private pure helper has two arguments. Must we introduce interfaces for every class, a DI container, a Builder and a Singleton service locator? Explain DI versus IoC and DIP, the smallest appropriate injection, and where composition-root guidance belongs.
evals.expected_output: Keep explicit callable/direct calls, distinguish DI/IoC/DIP, and reject mandatory abstractions/containers/service location while retaining existing construction ownership.
assertions: Recognizes existing callable injection and keeps trivial helpers direct.
Distinguishes DI from broader IoC and the Dependency Inversion Principle without requiring interfaces everywhere.
Rejects mandatory container/builder/service-locator machinery and reuses existing composition-root guidance.
